newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar drifts lower at close after quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar drifts lower at close after quiet trade.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar drifted lower at the close on Thursday after a quiet session and is not expected to move radically outside its new range before next week's Reserve Bank six monthly economic forecasts.
The currency ended at US$0.7011/18 from its 0.7025/30 open, having largely tracked its overnight range of 0.7010-25.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 68.87 from 68.96 at the open.
"We essentailly tracked the overnight range for the bulk of the day and I would imagine 10 points either side of that would probably cover it overnight as well," said one dealer.
"It seems to have lost a bit of steam but it doesn't look like it's going to come off too far either," he said.
People had largely adjusted their positions before next Thursday's eocnomic projections from the Reserve Bank.
"Before people look to open up any further large positions, I think they will wait and see what the Reserve Bank has to say. It's a bit of a lottery otherwise," he said.
